title: Shared CSI decoder with held-out-domain Mirror code
hypothesis: On unseen channel domains, a source-trained shared CSI decoder plus a low-dimensional persistent Mirror decoder coordinate can improve reconstruction and beamforming versus no domain adaptation at fixed latent feedback bits; it must beat matched ordinary embedding/FiLM/low-rank controls to support Mirror-specific attribution.
scope: Tiny linear CsiNet-style compressor on synthetic angular-delay MIMO channels; not a CsiNet implementation or PA291 reproduction.
data: Saleh-Valenzuela-inspired 8x8 complex angular-delay channels with random clustered paths; source domains train the shared decoder, target domain identities are held out, each target has 64 calibration and 256 test channels.
models: rank-1 Mirror decoder basis with one fitted domain coordinate
adaptation: All domain adaptation fits use only the 64 calibration channels per target. Test channels and target path draws are generated separately and are never used for fitting.
metrics: online latent and domain-ID feedback bits
CPU serialization plus held-out scoring wall time

storage.authority: actual torch.save inference payload bytes including shared encoder/decoder, adapter bases, codes, per-domain state and metadata
storage.feedback: 128 latent bits plus 2 domain-ID bits per channel for every method

success_gate: Mirror reaches within 1 dB NMSE of independent target decoder and >=95% of its beamforming rate in every fresh world, while using <=80% of matched ordinary-adapter total persistent bytes at identical feedback bits.
failure_gate: Any quality/byte gate missed or matched ordinary embedding/FiLM/LoRA reproduces Mirror within measurement precision.
boundaries: Synthetic channels only; no PA291 data or trained CsiNet checkpoint.
No multi-user interference, CSI coherence-time, RF energy or deployment latency claim.
Mirror domain coordinate is persistent at the decoder and counted in payload; it is not free online signaling.
Reported wall time covers serialization and held-out scoring only; common source fitting and calibration solves are excluded.
